events.region: Lauderdale, MS
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWJAN

The National Weather Service in Jackson has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southern Lauderdale County in east central Mississippi...

* Until 715 PM CDT.

* At 418 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Meridian, Marion, Nellieburg, Toomsuba, Zero, Causeyville and
Savoy.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
SMWMOB

The National Weather Service in Mobile has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Pensacola FL to Pascagoula MS out 20 NM...
Mississippi Sound...
North Mobile Bay...
South Mobile Bay...

* Until 545 PM CDT.

* At 412 PM CDT, a strong thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located near Farewell Buoy, moving north at 5
knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
East Fowl River Bridge, Sand Island Lighthouse, Bon Secour Bay,
Farewell Buoy, Middle Bay Light, Heron Bay, Point Clear, Weeks Bay,
Central Dauphin Island, and Fort Gaines.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southeastern Baker County in northeastern Florida...
Northern Duval County in northeastern Florida...
Southern Nassau County in northeastern Florida...

* WHEN...Until 630 PM EDT.

events.region: Baldwin, AL
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
TORMOB

The National Weather Service in Mobile has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
South central Baldwin County in southwestern Alabama...

* Until 430 PM CDT.

* At 401 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located 4 miles east of Fort Morgan, or 10 miles east of
Dauphin Island, moving northeast at 5 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed.
Damage to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree
damage is likely.

* This tornadic thunderstorm will remain over mainly rural areas of
south central Baldwin County.

SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Apalachee Bay or Coastal Waters From Keaton Beach to Ochlockonee
River Fl out to 20 Nm...
Coastal Waters From  Ochlockonee River to Apalachicola FL out to 20

Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 645 PM EDT.

* At 437 PM EDT, strong to severe thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line extending from 12 nm east of
V Tower to 37 nm south of S Tower, moving east at 20 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all

knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Buckeye Reef, O Tower, K Tower, S Tower, V Tower, Horseshoe Beach,
and Marker 24 Barge.
